_comment: Cell descriptor for layout/bin/compose-cell.py -- see layout/README.md
section 'Composing a gate' for the floorplan reasoning shared with every
other cell, and layout/sampler_tg/README.md for this cell's own result.
sampler_tg is a plain sky130 transmission gate: an 0.84/0.15 pfet and an
0.42/0.15 nfet whose drains are tied together (net 'a') and whose
sources are tied together (net 'b'), gated by independent control
signals (pfet gate 'ctrl', nfet gate 'ctrlb' -- normally clk/clkb, an
external complementary pair) rather than sharing one gate net the way
an inverter's pfet/nfet do. design/sampler_core.spice's sampler_dff
subckt draws this exact two-device shape four times, flat (no
sub-schematic symbol for it in design/xschem/sampler_dff.sch), so unlike
ro_stage/ro_nand2 there is no committed .subckt this cell's own LVS can
reference: lvs.reference below points at a hand-authored two-device
micro-netlist (sampler_tg.ref.spice, committed alongside this recipe)
matching the device-for-device shape sampler_dff.sch's TG_D/TG_FBM/
TG_S/TG_FBS instances share, not an xschem export.
Placement reuses ro_buf's own two-row stack (nfet at the origin, pfet
mirror_y directly above it, gates facing across the row gap) --
mirror_y flips the block's Y extent only (not X), so mn.U0_G and
mp.U0_G land at the SAME local x with no waypoint needed, exactly as in
ro_buf. What differs from ro_buf is which pins share a net: an inverter
ties both GATES together (net 'a') and lets each device's own SOURCE
go to its own supply tap; a transmission gate ties both DRAINS (net
'a', the same D-D route ro_buf's 'y' net already proves at x=1.9) and
both SOURCES together (net 'b', a short west-side vertical run at
x=0.1, well clear of the nwell/psub taps parked further west at
x=-2.0x) -- and leaves the two gates as two INDEPENDENT top-level pins
(ctrl/ctrlb) rather than one shared net. The taps supply bulk only (PMOS
well merge / NMOS substrate tie): their own TAP_N ports are promoted
directly as the 'vdd'/'vss' pins with no internal route to the device
row at all, since neither S/D pin is itself a supply node here.
